title: Marked compactification with a geometrically reduced radicial constant model
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $Z\subseteq X$ be nowhere dense and closed. There exist a proper finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline X$, a dense open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ over $k$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a nowhere dense closed subset $C\subseteq\overline X$ with $j^{-1}C=Z$. One can take $C=\overline{j(Z)}$. There also exists a finite purely inseparable extension $e/k$ [def-pc-field-tower], with $e=k$ in characteristic zero, such that $T=(\overline X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}e)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is nonempty, proper and finite type over $e$, and geometrically reduced over $e$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The canonical $k$-morphism $t:T\to\overline X$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], a homeomorphism on underlying spaces, and radicial [def-weil-radicial-morphism]. It therefore induces a bijection of component generic points [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point], with finite purely inseparable extensions of their residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. The inverse image $t^{-1}C$ is nowhere dense and closed. Both $\overline X$ and $T$ are Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth]), and each has finitely many irreducible components.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. By [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data] this gives $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$ with $p$ proper and $j$ an open immersion, scheme-theoretically dense. This implies topological density: a nonempty open disjoint from $j(X)$ would have its structure sheaf injecting into the zero sheaf, impossible at any of its nonzero local rings. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Nonemptiness follows from $X\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150, first two sentences; Nagata dense compactification

proof.text: Identify $X$ with the open $U=j(X)$ and put $C=\overline{j(Z)}$ in $\overline X$. Closure in an open subspace gives $C\cap U=\overline{j(Z)}^{\,U}=j(Z)$, since $Z$ is closed in $X$, so $j^{-1}C=Z$. If a nonempty open $V\subseteq\overline X$ were contained in $C$, density of $U$ would make $V\cap U$ a nonempty open subset of $U$ contained in $j(Z)$, contrary to the empty interior of $Z$. Thus $C$ is closed and nowhere dense. This argument also covers $Z=\varnothing$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150: replace the marking by its closure

proof.text: The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its single affine chart has a Noetherian ring, since a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, generated by $0$ and $1$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $\overline X$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finitely many irreducible components. Apply [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] to this locally finite-type scheme with finitely many components. It gives one finite purely inseparable $e/k$ for which $T=(\overline X_e)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is geometrically reduced over $e$. In characteristic zero this extension is $k$ by [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Tag 04KT, lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-reduced; Noetherian prerequisites: morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 and properties.tex Tag 0BA8

proof.text: Write $P=\overline X_e$, $i:T\to P$ for reduction, and $q:P\to\overline X$ for projection, so $t=q\circ i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $i$ is a surjective closed immersion and a universal homeomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], base change makes $P$ proper over $e$, and the closed immersion $i$ followed by this proper morphism makes $T$ proper over $e$. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The field $e$ is Noetherian by the same two-ideal argument as in step 3; hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] make $T$ Noetherian with finitely many irreducible components.

The map $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}e\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is universally injective by [lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective]. It is finite directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: both spectra have one point, and $e$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-module. By [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], its base change $q$ is finite and universally injective. The reduction $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]; it is universally injective since every one of its base changes is a homeomorphism. The composition clause of [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] now makes $t$ finite and universally injective, hence radicial by [def-weil-radicial-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01S4 (lemma-universally-injective), Tag 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite); base change and composition of finite and universally injective morphisms

proof.text: By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], $q$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces; reduction $i$ is one by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. Thus their composite $t$ is a homeomorphism. It follows that $T$ is nonempty, since $\overline X$ is nonempty. The inverse image $t^{-1}C$ is closed. Its interior is empty: any nonempty open inside it would map under the homeomorphism to a nonempty open inside $C$.

source.place: Tag 04KT proof, paragraph concerning the homeomorphism of reduced purely inseparable base change; inverse-image marking argument

proof.text: A homeomorphism carries maximal irreducible closed subsets bijectively to maximal irreducible closed subsets. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] each has a unique generic point, and the equality $t(\overline{\{\eta\}})=\overline{\{t(\eta)\}}$ shows that these points correspond under $t$. By radiciality [def-weil-radicial-morphism], the residue extensions at these points are purely inseparable.

source.place: Tag 04KT proof: corresponding component generic points; morphisms.tex Tag 01S4

proof.text: For completeness their residue extensions are finite without any reducedness assumption on $\overline X$. Around $y=t(x)$ take an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Finiteness of $t$ gives its inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ generated by finitely many elements as an $A$-module. For the primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ of $y,x$, the same generators span $D=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The prime quotient $D/\mathfrak r$ associated to $\mathfrak q$ is a finite-dimensional domain over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, hence a field: multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space and is therefore surjective. Its fraction field is thus itself; by the localization and residue-field definitions it is $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Consequently $[\kappa(x):\kappa(t(x))]<\infty$. Apply this to the component generic points from step 7.
